plate_mesh_from_image — DRIVE roadjp op

• Data kinds: rgba → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.plate_mesh_from_image(rgba, width: 'float', height: 'float', *, cell: 'int' = 4, thickness: 'float' = 0.004, back_color=(0.55, 0.55, 0.55), label: 'int' = 4) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import roadjp; roadjp.plate_mesh_from_image(rgba, width: 'float', height: 'float', *, cell: 'int' = 4, thickness: 'float' = 0.004, back_color=(0.55, 0.55, 0.55), label: 'int' = 4) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("plate_mesh_from_image"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Turns an RGBA image into the mesh of a thin plate carrying the face colors.

The image is cut into tiles of cell × cell pixels, and only tiles whose mean alpha is 0.5 or more become faces (2 triangles). Face colour = the alpha-weighted mean colour of the tile Σ(α·rgb) / Σα. The front normal = −x (facing a car approaching in +x at yaw 0); the back has the same shape with back_color (normal +x). Origin = centre of the plate; the plate lies in the y-z plane (image left = +y, top = +z); the thickness thickness is spread ±half along x. Unused vertices are not kept (so that dimensions can be measured from the vertices).

Return value {"V", "F", "color", "label", "front_faces": (0, n), "back_faces": (n, 2n), "cells": (rows, cols)}. Empty input (rgba with 0 elements) raises ValueError.
